title: Comparative chart of the ancient and modern navigators
creator: John Ross
description: The folding chart at the front of Ross's narrative, laying the tracks of the older navigators over those of the modern ones in red across North America, Baffin's Bay, Hudson's Bay and the Pacific - Ross's argument for what remained to be found.

title: The Victory in a gale
creator: John Ross
description: The paddle steamer Victory, the first steam vessel taken into the Arctic, labouring in a heavy sea on the outward passage of 1829.

title: Taking possession
creator: John Ross
description: The landing party taking formal possession of the new coast, with the ship and boats in the bay behind - the ceremony that made Boothia Felix British on paper.

title: Plan of Elizabeth Harbour
creator: John Ross
description: A surveyed plan of Elizabeth Harbour on the Boothia coast, with soundings and the bearings taken from the ship.

title: Andrew's Island
creator: John Ross
description: Hand-coloured plate of the Victory close under the cliffs of Andrew's Island among broken floe ice, lithographed by Chevalier from Ross's own drawing.

title: Cape Margaret
creator: John Ross
description: A boat party under the cliffs at Cape Margaret on the Boothia shore.

title: The Victory among the ice
creator: John Ross
description: The Victory working through loose ice in Prince Regent Inlet under sail and steam.

title: Table of latitudes and positions, p. 209
creator: John Ross
description: A ruled table of observed latitudes from the narrative - the positions on which the whole survey of Boothia rests.

title: Account of the daily proportion of provisions served to 18 men for 14 days
creator: John Ross
description: The ration table of the Victory: what eighteen men were issued, item by item, for a fortnight. Ross printed it to show how the ship was kept on reduced allowance through four winters in the ice, and it is the plainest record in the book of what an Arctic crew actually ate.

title: Felix Harbour
creator: John Ross
description: Hand-coloured plate of the Victory in her first winter quarters at Felix Harbour, Boothia, the ensign flying from a staff on the ice under a dark winter sky.

title: First communication with the Netsilingmiut
creator: John Ross
description: Hand-coloured plate of the first meeting, in January 1830, between the Victory's people and the Netsilingmiut who came out to the ship with their sledges - the beginning of the four-year relationship on which the expedition's survival and much of its geography depended.

title: North Hendon
creator: John Ross
description: Hand-coloured plate of the Inuit snow village Ross called North Hendon, its domes built on a rise with the people and dogs outside.

title: Ikmallik and Apelagliu drawing the chart
creator: John Ross
description: Hand-coloured plate of the cabin of the Victory with Ikmallik and Apelagliu at the table among the officers, drawing for Ross the coast of their own country. It is the making of the chart on the next plate, and one of the frankest images in the literature of an expedition being told where it was.

title: Chart drawn by the natives
creator: Ikmallik and Apelagliu
description: The chart of the Gulf of Boothia, King William's Land, Neitchille and the isthmus, drawn by Inuit for Ross and engraved from the original in his possession. Ross's note on the plate says the marks show where the Boothians said huts or villages stood on their journey to Neitchille. It is Indigenous geographical knowledge printed as a map, and the coastline it gives is substantially right.

title: Group of Netsilingmiut
creator: John Ross
description: Hand-coloured plate of a group of Netsilingmiut in winter clothing, standing on the ice.

title: Plan of Felix Harbour, 1830
creator: John Ross
description: The surveyed plan of Felix Harbour where the Victory lay through the first winter, with the ship's berth marked and the soundings taken round her.

title: Quingmak
creator: John Ross
description: Hand-coloured plate captioned Quingmak, lithographed from Ross's original drawing: a Boothia landscape with hunters and game.

title: Lady Melville's Lake
creator: John Ross
description: The lake on the Boothia isthmus crossed by the sledge parties, with a party and their dogs on the shore.

title: Victory Point
creator: John Ross
description: The cairn at Victory Point on the north-west shore of King William's Land, reached and named by James Clark Ross on 29 May 1830. Fifteen years later Franklin's people would leave their record within a few miles of this spot.

title: Cape Adelaide and Sheriff's Harbour
creator: John Ross
description: The Victory in her second winter quarters at Sheriff's Harbour with a dog team on the ice and a crescent moon over Cape Adelaide, near which James Clark Ross fixed the North Magnetic Pole on 1 June 1831.

title: Sledge party in a frozen ravine
creator: John Ross
description: A sledge party hauling up a deep frozen stream bed between rock walls, on one of the Boothia journeys.

title: The pillar
creator: John Ross
description: A great isolated rock on the Boothia coast with sledges and dogs halted beneath it.

title: The River Lindsay
creator: John Ross
description: An Inuit camp of skin tents beside the River Lindsay, with people and dogs.

title: The Victory
creator: John Ross
description: The Victory among heavy ice with a boat party working alongside, late in the expedition. She was abandoned in Victoria Harbour in May 1832 and the crews walked north to Fury Beach.

title: Surveyed plan of a Boothia harbour
creator: John Ross
description: One of the surveyed harbour plans at the end of the narrative, with soundings, the compass rose and the shoreline traced from the boat survey.
